subject: Request: Updated Third-Party Inventory + Cloud Provider Change Notice
messages:
From: Jane Porter <jane.porter@bighealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bighealth.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Updated third-party inventory + notice of provider change

Hi Karthik,

Hope youre well. As part of our procurement closeout and upcoming security review for BigHealths vendor consolidation, we need an up-to-date list of Redwoods subprocessors (vendor roster) and a short summary of any planned cloud/provider changes in the next 90 days that could affect data residency, processing locations, or subcontractors.

Specifically:
- Complete vendor inventory CSV or PDF (name, purpose, countries processed, subprocessed data types)
- Any planned migrations or provider swaps (e.g., moving regions, adding third-party caching/CDN, new storage providers) with anticipated dates
- Confirmation of SOC 2 / ISO certifications for primary providers and whether evidence can be shared under NDA

Were targeting a compliance review next week (week of 6/15). Can you share the above by EOD Thursday 6/10? If you have a single-file package (inventory + assurance matrix) that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Jane Porter
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
BigHealth Systems

Attachments: None

Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:36:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Updated third-party inventory + notice of provider change

Jane,

Thanks for the heads up. Were on it. Ill pull the most recent subprocessor inventory and loop in Legal and Security to confirm what evidence we can share under NDA.

Quick notes: we have a planned optimization rollout for certain edge caching partners in mid-June that should be non-custodial, and a staggered pilot to add an additional EU storage partner (for customers who opt into EU-only pinning). Neither should affect primary production data for BigHealth, but Ill confirm exact timelines and locations.

Ill get a consolidated package over to you by EOD 6/10 as requested.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Confirming the assurance matrix attached. Key notes for BigHealth:
- Edge caching partner (EdgeCloudX): non-custodial, only serves cached model responses; processing occurs in region requested by customer routing policy; no persistent storage of customer prompts.
- EU storage pilot (NordStore): will only contain customer-chosen pinned assets; default production remains in existing primary regions (us-east-1).
- Primary compute remains on our contracted public cloud (ProviderA) for production workloads; no planned migration of production compute in the next 90 days.

Attached: SOC2-TypeII-Report-2026.pdf (we can provide the full report under Acknowledgement receipt as Laura noted). Ive added a column in the matrix showing whether evidence can be shared immediately or requires Acknowledgement.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of InfoSec
Redwood Inference

Please find the consolidated package attached: the Redwood subprocessor inventory (redwood_subprocessor_inventory_202606.pdf), the cloud migration assurance matrix (cloud_migration_assurance_matrix.xlsx), and the SOC 2 summary pages. Per our NDA, we can provide the full SOC 2 report immediately after a simple Acknowledgement of Receipt (link to DocuSign below).

Summary highlights:
- No planned migration of primary production compute in the next 90 days; ProviderA remains primary.
- Edge caching partner (EdgeCloudX) is non-custodial; impacts are limited to response caching and do not introduce persistent customer data storage.
- EU storage pilot (NordStore) is a customer-opt-in pilot scheduled to start 2026-06-18; it will host pinned customer assets only if explicitly opted in.
